Thank you for coming, Patrícia. I have twenty minutes, and I have never seen a review from your team. Start with the headline.
The headline is this: Northwind is a customer whose usage has come back. The two teams that had stopped using the platform are active again.
Good. And remind me who you are. David mentioned you, but I do not know your role.
I am the Customer Success Manager who looks after your account. I am the person you call when something is not working.
Fine. I am the decision-maker on this renewal, so give me one number that I can use with my board.
The workflow that your warehouse team uses now takes eleven minutes less per order. That is where most of the cost savings come from.
And the benchmark? How do we compare with companies like us?
Your efficiency is above the benchmark for logistics companies, which is the strongest argument for the renewal.

Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. A few things about tomorrow's business review at Northwind. Richard Moore is the new executive sponsor who took over in February, so he has never met you and he has never seen our numbers. He is a man whose calendar is full from eight to eight, so you will get twenty minutes, not an hour. Open with the headline, which is simple: usage has come back on every team. Then give him three numbers, not ten. The first is the footprint. Last year we were in three teams, and today we are in six, including finance. The second is the time that the warehouse team saves on every order. The third is the benchmark, which shows that Northwind is doing better than similar companies. Do not explain the product. Richard is not the person who uses it. He is the person who pays for it.

Patrícia, it is David. A quick tip about Richard, because I have worked with him for six years. Richard is a person who reads the last slide first. He wants to know the decision that you need from him, so put it at the top. He also hates words that he cannot measure. If you say better, he will ask better than what. If you say faster, he will ask how many minutes. And one more thing. Richard came from a company where they consolidated five tools into one, so he likes vendors who make things simpler, not bigger. Tell him that our platform replaced two spreadsheets and an old reporting tool, which is true, and he will listen. Keep it short, and please do not read the slides to him.
